explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1097 and its negative resolution of 'always O(n^{3/2})?'. Via the equivalence with Bourgain's sums-differences problem, the achievable exponent is at least 1.77898 > 3/2. The set of common differences includes both d and -d, because d ≠ 0 is not required to be positive. This at most doubles the count, so it does not affect the O(n^{3/2}) question.
